fields.hero_description: Build a document approval workflow that sends each draft to the right approvers and ties every approval to one version.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Document Approval Workflow
fields.features_subheading: Each workflow decides who reviews a draft and which version their approval covers.
fields.feature_1:
Approvers in order, or all at once

Some documents need one approver after another; others need several at the same time. Set the order per document type, and add conditions, such as legal review for a new client.
fields.feature_2:
Each approval covers one version

An approval applies to the exact version the approver opened. If anyone edits the document afterward, that approval is cleared and the new version goes back to the same approver.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders first, then a delegate

Choose how long each approver has before a reminder arrives in Slack or by email, and who takes over after that. A review that stalls moves on without anyone chasing it.
fields.feature_4:
AI reads documents as they arrive

An AI step turns each uploaded document into fields, such as its owner and revision number. Any field it cannot read with confidence goes to a person before the document is routed.
fields.feature_5:
A live board of what waits on whom

The dashboard lists every open review, who holds it, and how long it has waited, updated as decisions land. Each decision is saved to a database you own, with its version.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

Export the approval app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans, with every route and reminder. Engineers can review the rules like other code and change them.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Documents That Wait on Approval
fields.tab_content_1:
QA approves Rev 4 before it replaces Rev 3

Halima Josten uploads Rev 4 of SOP-114, the allergen changeover procedure at Thistlebank Dairy. Ezio Abaya, the production lead, approves it first. It then waits for Wenona Kashyap, the QA manager. Rev 3 stays the effective version until she approves, and her decision is saved with the time.
fields.tab_content_2:
Drawing QM-2207 waits on its last approver

Quellmark Robotics sends Rev C of drawing QM-2207, a motor bracket, to design, manufacturing, and quality at once. It is released only when all 3 approve. So far 2 of 3 have: Anselm Rautio in design and Liv Haraldsen in manufacturing. Until Teodoro Malvar in quality approves, the shop keeps building to Rev B.
fields.tab_content_3:
A stalled report passes to the partner's delegate

Lamberth Oyelaran Engineers' warehouse roof survey needs a partner's approval before it goes out. A report with no decision after 48 hours goes to a delegate. The partner, Ottilie Vasquez, has not opened it in 48 hours. The app sends it to her delegate, Rashid Iturbe, in a direct message with the report attached.
fields.tab_content_4:
One budget change sends v4 back to finance

Agathe Delacroix, finance director at Coldbrook Youth Trust, approved v3 of a grant proposal on Monday. On Tuesday, Saoirse Ketterley raises the equipment line from $9,800 to $12,400. The edit clears her approval and sends v4 back with the changed line marked. It cannot go to the funder until she approves.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Document Approval Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to map a document approval workflow, build it with Emergent, and test it on drafts you have already approved.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the documents that wait longest
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Describe each route in a sentence
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every document type that waits on someone before it can be used: procedures, drawings, client reports, proposals. Next to each, note who approves it today and the longest it waited last quarter. The type with the longest wait is your starting point.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write one sentence per document type that names a person or a role at every step, such as the production lead and then the QA manager. Emergent builds the app and its routing logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick two deadlines for every approver: one for a reminder and a longer one for handing the document to a delegate. Use numbers your team can meet, such as 24 hours and 48 hours, and name each delegate in advance.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the drive or document system that holds your drafts through its API. The app then reads the current version from the source, not a copy someone attached to an email, and records each decision against that version.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide what happens when an approver says no. Send the document back to its author with the comment, then choose whether the revised version restarts at the first approver or returns to the one who rejected it. Set one rule per document type.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run five documents from last month through the workflow before going live. Check that each reached the right approvers in the right order, and edit one after approval to confirm its approval clears. Fix a rule by prompting, then run all five again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live with one document type
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch on that first document type and keep the rest on the old process for 2 weeks. Compare approval times with the 2 weeks before, read every reassignment to a delegate, then move the next type over.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a document approval workflow that runs on its own and logs every step.

faq_plan.q: What is the workflow for document approval?
faq_plan.ref: What is the workflow for document approval?

prov.original: What is the workflow for document approval?

faq_plan.a: A document approval workflow is the sequence of reviews, checks, and sign-offs a document passes through before it counts as final. An author submits a draft, named approvers review it, and the approved version is released. Routing can be serial, parallel, or conditional: one approver after another, several at once, or a route picked by the document's details.

faq_plan.q: How to design document approval workflows with exception handling?
faq_plan.ref: how to design document approval workflows with exception handling
faq_plan.a: Map the normal route first, then add one rule for each way it breaks: no answer, a rejection, an edit after approval, or an approver who leaves the company. Give each rule an owner and a deadline. In Emergent's AI automation builder, you write those rules in plain English, and Emergent builds the app that runs them, alerts included.

faq_plan.q: How AI agents make decisions in document approval workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how ai agents make decisions in document approval workflows
faq_plan.a: They should not make the final call: an AI agent reads and sorts, and your written rules and a named approver decide. The agent pulls out the document's type and client, and the rules pick the route from those values. Save what the agent read next to each approval for anyone checking it later. Apps built with Emergent can include that AI reading step.

faq_plan.q: How organizations automate document approvals workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how organizations automate document approvals workflows
faq_plan.a: They move the route out of email and into software. Uploading a document starts the workflow, rules pick the approvers, reminders replace follow-up emails, and each decision is stored against the version it covers. Producing the draft in the first place, by filling a template from a record, is document automation, and it can hand each new draft straight to the approval route.

faq_plan.q: How AI reduces bottlenecks in automated document approval workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how ai reduces bottlenecks in automated document approval workflows
flagged: PA6 asker unclear: headline (how X does Y)
faq_plan.a: AI cuts the wait before an approver ever sees the document. It reads the type, the client, and the amount on upload, so the rules route each file at once instead of after someone sorts it by hand. The decision stays with a person, and a reminder goes out when a step runs past its deadline.

faq_plan.q: How to automate document approval workflows in my business?
faq_plan.ref: how to automate document approval workflows in my business
faq_plan.a: Automate it around one owner: a person who knows every route and can change a rule the day a policy changes. Keep the written rules where staff can read them, and check the average wait per document type each month. In Emergent, that owner changes a rule by describing the new one in a prompt.

faq_plan.q: How to set up document approval workflows?
faq_plan.ref: how to set up document approval workflows
faq_plan.a: Set one up per document type by deciding four things: what starts it, who approves and in what order, how long each step may take, and which version an approval covers. Write those down before you build anything. Purchase orders add one more input, an amount that picks the approvers, and purchase order automation covers that case.

faq_plan.q: What should a document approval workflow system record?
faq_plan.a: It should record four details for every decision: who decided, which version they saw, when, and any comment. Keep rejected versions as well as approved ones. That record answers the question a client or an auditor asks months later: who approved this exact text, and when.

faq_plan.q: Do I need dedicated document approval workflow software?
faq_plan.a: No, not for a handful of documents a month: a shared folder with a checklist can hold up. Once you need reminders, delegates, or a record per version, use software. Check whether each tool charges for people who only approve. Emergent has no per-approver seats.

faq_plan.q: How does an approval workflow fit into document management?
faq_plan.a: It is the part that decides when a stored draft becomes the approved version. Document management is a system or process used to capture, track, and store electronic documents; the approval workflow adds who must approve it and by when. Let only the latest draft enter the route, and keep every earlier version on file.

plan.angle: The top 10 are document-management and e-signature vendors defining the term, plus Microsoft's approvals docs. This page draws four document cases where an email chain breaks: an SOP revision that must not take effect before QA approves, a drawing released only when all 3 approvers agree, a client report reassigned after 48 hours without a decision, and a grant proposal whose approval is cleared by a later edit. The FAQ covers exception handling, the role of AI, setup and where approval sits in document management.
